The issue ultimately boils down to empirical verification. If I claim that I know a quantity to some extreme degree of precision, yet I lack the ability to measure quantities to such precision, then my claim of high precision is "unfalsifiable", incapable of being verified and thus not empirically trustworthy.

This is one of the VERY many areas in which #tech and #programming geeks, who generally have been allowed to get away with an extreme degree of _innumeracy_ (i.e. lack of fundamental understanding of maths) because they trust their computers to do all their calculations, have demonstrated their ignorance: they're constantly making basic errors of precision in dealing with numerical quantities, because they want to have a practically *religious* and irrational degree of faith in the objective truth of all numerical quantities.

(etc.)
